summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE and RFA, was admitted for abdominal pain, vomiting with blood-streaked emesis, and abdominal distension. Evaluation revealed stable vital signs, no active bleeding, and mild acute kidney injury likely due to reduced oral intake. Imaging showed no ascites, bowel obstruction, or new malignancy. Symptoms were attributed to gastritis and portal gastropathy. He improved with supportive care, rehydration, and continuation of home medications. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged home with plans to follow up with Transplant Hepatology and primary care for ongoing management.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Angiodysplasia of intestine (without mention of hemorrhage)
Other specified disorders of stomach and duodenum
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, in remission
